safety.title: Safety Reminders
safety.disclaimer: Always check the weather before heading out. Wear appropriate footwear and clothing. Stay hydrated and bring water. Tell someone where you are going. If you feel dizzy, short of breath, or experience chest pain, stop immediately and seek help.

walk_neighborhood.name: Neighborhood Walk
walk_neighborhood.description: A gentle stroll around your neighborhood at a comfortable pace.
tips: Wear comfortable shoes with good support
Start with 10 minutes and build up gradually
Walk on well-lit sidewalks or paths
Bring a phone for safety
walk_neighborhood.safetyTip: Avoid walking during extreme heat or icy conditions.

walk_park.name: Park Walk
walk_park.description: A moderate-paced walk through a local park or green space.
tips: Choose a park with paved or flat paths
Walk at a pace where you can still talk but feel slightly breathless
Enjoy the scenery — it boosts mood
Try to include some gentle inclines
walk_park.safetyTip: Stay on marked paths and let someone know your route.

walk_nature_trail.name: Nature Trail Walk
walk_nature_trail.description: A longer walk on a nature trail with varied terrain.
tips: Choose a trail rated easy to moderate
Wear sturdy walking shoes or boots
Bring water and a snack for longer walks
Use trekking poles for extra stability
walk_nature_trail.safetyTip: Check trail conditions before you go and don't walk alone in remote areas.

fast_walk_interval.name: Interval Fast Walk
fast_walk_interval.description: Alternate between normal and brisk walking to boost cardio fitness.
tips: Walk normally for 2 minutes, then briskly for 1 minute
Swing your arms naturally to increase pace
Focus on good posture — chin up, shoulders back
Gradually increase the brisk intervals
fast_walk_interval.safetyTip: Slow down if you feel too breathless to speak a short sentence.

fast_walk_poles.name: Pole Walking
fast_walk_poles.description: Walking with poles engages the upper body and improves balance.
tips: Use poles at the right height — elbows at 90 degrees
Plant the pole opposite to the stepping foot
Keep a natural rhythm
Poles reduce strain on knees and hips
fast_walk_poles.safetyTip: Learn proper pole technique to avoid wrist strain.

nordic_walking.name: Nordic Walking
nordic_walking.description: A vigorous full-body walking technique using specialized poles.
tips: Take a class to learn proper Nordic walking form
Use Nordic-specific poles with wrist straps
Engage your core and push through each stride
It burns 20–40% more calories than regular walking
nordic_walking.safetyTip: Start slowly and master the technique before increasing speed.

jog_easy.name: Easy Jog
jog_easy.description: A gentle jog at a conversational pace for cardiovascular health.
tips: Run at a pace where you can still hold a conversation
Land softly with a midfoot strike
Start with short jog intervals if you're new to running
Good running shoes are essential
jog_easy.safetyTip: Consult your doctor before starting a jogging program, especially if you have joint issues.

jog_walk_intervals.name: Jog–Walk Intervals
jog_walk_intervals.description: Alternate between jogging and walking to build endurance gradually.
tips: Try 1 minute jogging, 2 minutes walking
Increase jog time gradually over weeks
Walk briskly during walking intervals
This method is proven safe and effective for beginners
jog_walk_intervals.safetyTip: Stop jogging and walk if you feel any joint pain or discomfort.

cycle_leisure.name: Leisure Cycling
cycle_leisure.description: A relaxed bike ride on flat terrain at a comfortable pace.
tips: Adjust your seat so your leg is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal
Start on flat paths away from traffic
Wear a helmet always
A recumbent or step-through bike is easiest to mount
cycle_leisure.safetyTip: Always wear a helmet and use lights/reflectors when cycling.

cycle_path.name: Cycle Path Ride
cycle_path.description: A moderate ride along a dedicated cycling path.
tips: Plan your route using cycling paths or quiet roads
Keep a steady moderate pace
Signal your turns to other path users
Bring water for rides over 20 minutes
cycle_path.safetyTip: Check your brakes and tire pressure before each ride.

cycle_hills.name: Hill Cycling
cycle_hills.description: A challenging ride including hills for vigorous cardiovascular exercise.
tips: Shift to a lower gear before the hill
Stand on the pedals briefly for steep sections
Control speed on downhills with gentle braking
Build up to hills gradually over several weeks
cycle_hills.safetyTip: Avoid steep descents until you are confident with braking.

swim_laps.name: Lap Swimming
swim_laps.description: Swimming laps in a pool at a steady pace for full-body exercise.
tips: Choose a pool with a shallow end for comfort
Start with a few laps and rest between them
Backstroke and breaststroke are gentler on shoulders
Swimming is excellent for joint health
swim_laps.safetyTip: Never swim alone and always use a pool with a lifeguard.

swim_aqua_walk.name: Aqua Walking
swim_aqua_walk.description: Walking in waist-deep water for low-impact resistance exercise.
tips: Walk in waist to chest-deep water
The water provides natural resistance
Move your arms through the water for upper body work
Excellent for those with arthritis or joint pain
swim_aqua_walk.safetyTip: Use pool handrails when entering and exiting.

hike_easy.name: Easy Hike
hike_easy.description: A moderate hike on well-maintained trails with gentle elevation.
tips: Choose trails rated easy with well-marked paths
Wear hiking boots with ankle support
Bring plenty of water, snacks, and a hat
Use trekking poles for stability on uneven ground
hike_easy.safetyTip: Tell someone your hiking plan and expected return time.

garden_active.name: Active Gardening
garden_active.description: Gardening activities like digging, weeding, raking, and carrying supplies.
tips: Alternate between tasks to use different muscles
Use raised beds or kneeling pads to reduce strain
Take breaks every 20 minutes
Gardening burns more calories than you think!
garden_active.safetyTip: Wear gloves, sun protection, and stay hydrated.

outdoor_tai_chi.name: Outdoor Tai Chi
outdoor_tai_chi.description: Practicing tai chi in a park or garden for balance and mindfulness.
tips: Find a flat, peaceful area in a park or garden
Practice in the morning for a calm start to the day
Wear loose, comfortable clothing
Join a local outdoor tai chi group for motivation
outdoor_tai_chi.safetyTip: Choose a surface that is flat and not slippery.
